description: Closed-box hardware/embedded device test case catalogue. Interface-organized test cases covering physical, network, USB, serial, display, RFID, CAN bus, Zigbee, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, UWB, JTAG/debug, memory, OS/application, PCAP analysis, and cloud/vendor assessment of embedded devices.

test_cases.title: Boot to Live OS
methodology: Connect tester-controlled bootable removable media to each exposed USB interface.
Attempt startup using the device's documented or standard boot-selection controls.
Determine whether removable media can load an alternate operating system or otherwise bypass normal device startup controls.

test_cases.title: Boot Menu / Firmware Access
methodology: Initiate device startup and use standard firmware-entry and boot-selection key sequences.
Determine whether firmware setup, boot-order, and alternate-boot controls are accessible.
Assess whether access to administrative firmware settings requires authorization.

test_cases.title: Boot Recovery Behavior
methodology: Exercise approved failed-start and recovery-key sequences without intentionally damaging device state.
Allow the device to complete normal recovery or startup behavior after each attempt.
Confirm whether the system returns to the intended operating and application state.

test_cases.title: Offline Disk Access
methodology: Use an approved alternate-boot path to access attached storage outside normal operating-system controls.
Determine whether the internal disk can be mounted, read, or copied without valid operating-system authentication.
Do not open the enclosure or remove storage unless physical tampering is explicitly in scope.

test_cases.title: Offline Registry / Credential Access
methodology: Use approved offline operating-system access to inspect protected registry hives and credential stores.
Determine whether account hashes, secrets, or configuration data can be accessed without valid credentials.
Avoid changes to source media or credentials unless explicitly authorized.

test_cases.title: Offline Account Modification
methodology: Use approved offline access to evaluate whether local account data may be altered.
Perform only reversible test changes under written authorization.
Confirm whether normal startup authentication controls can be bypassed or modified.

test_cases.title: Controlled Persistence / Remote Access
methodology: Use an approved controlled-host path to evaluate whether a temporary remote-access mechanism can be installed.
Limit testing to reversible, documented artifacts and customer-approved callback infrastructure.
Confirm whether the artifact persists or enables remote device control across normal restart conditions.

categories.name: Network Attack Surface and Vulnerability Review

test_cases.title: Service Discovery
methodology: Identify TCP and UDP services reachable through exposed Ethernet interfaces from authorized test positions.
Record reachable ports, service fingerprints, and protocol metadata.
Compare observed exposure to expected network-segmentation and device-function requirements.

test_cases.title: Vulnerability Scan
methodology: Perform authorized vulnerability and configuration scans against exposed device interfaces.
Correlate scanner output with targeted service verification to distinguish actionable weaknesses from informational results.
Record confirmed exposures and evidence for reporting.

test_cases.title: VNC Exposure
methodology: Identify VNC/RFB listener exposure and supported protocol and security options.
Test authentication negotiation and unauthenticated connection behavior without accessing an unauthorized session.
Determine whether remote-display exposure aligns with intended device administration.

test_cases.title: VNC Session Confidentiality
methodology: Capture and inspect VNC connection traffic during approved connection attempts.
Evaluate protection of authentication exchange, screen content, keyboard input, clipboard data, and session traffic.
Record whether the protocol provides encryption appropriate to the intended use.

test_cases.title: SMB Exposure
methodology: Identify SMB service exposure and supported protocol dialects.
Assess signing, guest or null-session behavior, authentication requirements, and information available through unauthenticated negotiation.
Determine whether SMB exposure aligns with expected management requirements.

test_cases.title: WinRM/RPC Exposure
methodology: Identify Windows RPC, endpoint-mapper, dynamic RPC, and WinRM or WS-Management services exposed through Ethernet.
Assess unauthenticated reachability and service metadata.
Determine whether management-service exposure provides a reportable security condition.

test_cases.title: Legacy Web/VNC Viewer Exposure
methodology: Review web-accessible remote-viewer components and associated downloadable client artifacts.
Inspect server responses, page metadata, and client-side resources for legacy technology, unsupported dependencies, and exposed service information.
Determine whether the viewer interface introduces a reportable exposure.

test_cases.title: VNC Credential Testing
methodology: Conduct authorized, rate-controlled password validation against exposed VNC services using approved account and password candidates.
Monitor authentication behavior and agreed stop conditions throughout testing.
Record successful authentication only when it results from an authorized test credential attempt.

test_cases.title: SMB Credential Testing
methodology: Conduct authorized, rate-controlled SMB authentication validation using approved account and password candidates.
Apply agreed attempt limits and stop conditions consistent with observed or documented lockout controls.
Record successful authentication and affected account context.

test_cases.title: Local Session / Kiosk Escape Behavior
methodology: Observe startup and intended application behavior after local physical access is obtained.
Use approved keyboard, mouse, and HID interactions to test application boundaries, accessibility surfaces, and standard operating-system escape sequences.
Determine whether a physically present user can reach an unauthorized operating-system or command-execution context.

test_cases.title: Ethernet Drop Abuse
methodology: Disconnect and reconnect the exposed Ethernet link, or insert approved passive or intermediate network equipment.
Observe device, application, and network behavior for operational or security alerts.
Determine whether physical Ethernet access creates an independent attacker foothold or data-collection opportunity.

test_cases.title: Pivot After Device Control
methodology: If authorized device control is established, assess network reachability from the controlled device to adjacent in-scope systems.
Limit discovery and validation to approved target ranges and protocols.
Determine whether the device can be used to access otherwise segmented network resources.

test_cases.title: Egress / Call-Home Simulation
methodology: If an approved controlled-host path is established, initiate a benign outbound callback to tester-controlled infrastructure.
Observe egress controls, network monitoring, and device behavior.
Confirm whether the device can establish outbound communications outside expected operational channels.

test_cases.title: Passive Boot/Idle Capture
methodology: Capture network traffic during device startup, normal operation, and idle periods from an authorized observation point.
Inspect traffic for cleartext credentials, commands, tokens, hostnames, service metadata, and unencrypted application communication.
Correlate relevant observations with exposed services and intended network behavior.

test_cases.title: O.MG/HID Injection While Logged Out
methodology: Connect an approved HID-emulation device while the system is at the lock screen, user chooser, or accessibility interface.
Deliver benign, documented input sequences to assess focus behavior, accessibility interactions, and navigation controls.
Determine whether accepted HID input permits passwordless access, unauthorized action, or security-boundary bypass.

test_cases.title: O.MG/HID Injection During Active Session
methodology: Connect an approved HID-emulation device during an active application session.
Deliver benign, documented input sequences to assess whether the application or operating-system boundary can be exited.
Determine whether accepted HID input reaches a shell, administrative interface, or other unauthorized execution context.

test_cases.title: Boot-Time USB Interaction
methodology: Connect approved keyboard or HID-emulation devices during startup.
Use benign input sequences to assist standard boot-key interaction.
Determine whether boot-time HID acceptance changes firmware, recovery, or alternate-boot access.

test_cases.title: USB Network Interface / Traffic Exposure
methodology: Connect an approved USB network-interface device to each exposed USB port.
Establish an isolated, tester-controlled network path and observe interface enumeration, address assignment, and device behavior.
Validate whether the interface enables traffic observation, network access, or remote-management reachability without device authorization.

test_cases.title: Azure IoT Call-Home
methodology: Capture network traffic during startup and idle operation to identify device-initiated cloud or management communications.
Inspect transport security, endpoint metadata, certificate behavior, payload handling, and sensitive-data exposure.
Determine whether outbound communications disclose information or provide an unauthorized control path.

test_cases.title: Local Name / Service Disclosure
methodology: Passively capture local network traffic from an authorized network observation point.
Identify local discovery, name-resolution, SMB or browser-service, and host-identification traffic.
Determine whether unauthenticated observers can derive device identity, role, or service information.

test_cases.title: Physical Interface Inventory and Port Mapping
methodology: Visually inspect all exposed physical interfaces on the device.
Document interface types, connectors, physical controls, indicators, and labels.
Compare observed interfaces against vendor-supplied documentation and specifications.
Note any undocumented or unexpected interfaces for further investigation.

test_cases.title: Passive Traffic Baseline and Active-Interface Discovery
methodology: Mirror all Ethernet interfaces using a port-mirroring switch or passive tap.
Capture traffic with Wireshark or tcpdump during startup, idle, normal operation, and shutdown phases.
Review captures for active IP addresses, MAC addresses, protocols, services, and peer endpoints.
Compare observed traffic against vendor documentation and expected network behavior.
Perform limited active discovery to confirm interface configurations and reachability.

test_cases.title: Audio Injection
methodology: Connect a 3.5mm-to-RCA cable from a tester-controlled laptop to the device line-in or audio input.
Play audio tones and recordings at varying volumes through the connected input.
Observe whether injected audio is captured, recorded, replayed, or disrupts normal device operation.
Document any change in device behavior resulting from external audio input.

test_cases.title: Interactive Serial Session Attempt
methodology: Connect a USB-to-serial adapter to exposed serial interfaces.
Configure the terminal emulator for common baud rates (115200, 57600, 19200, 9600) and bit parameters (8-N-1, 7-E-1).
Attempt to affect device startup by sending character sequences, toggling DTR, and sending Break signals.
Determine whether serial input permits interactive access to a shell, bootloader, or diagnostic interface.

test_cases.title: Serial Port Snooping
methodology: Connect a USB-to-serial adapter or passive serial splitter to the exposed serial port.
Configure the terminal emulator for expected baud rates and parameters.
Monitor for serial traffic during power-on, normal operation, and shutdown.
Try alternate baud rates if captured data appears corrupted or unintelligible.
Record all observed traffic for analysis.

test_cases.title: Serial Traffic Sensitive-Content Analysis
methodology: Decode framed messages from serial captures using protocol-appropriate tools.
Search decoded data for device identifiers, credentials, patient data, configuration secrets, and authentication tokens.
Document any sensitive content transmitted over the serial interface.

test_cases.title: Unauthenticated Vulnerability Scanning
methodology: Connect to the device network segment from the authorized test position.
Determine the device IP address through passive observation or approved active discovery.
Scan the device with automated vulnerability scanners without providing any credentials.
Review and document scan results for confirmed vulnerabilities.

test_cases.title: Authenticated Vulnerability Scanning
methodology: Obtain valid device credentials through approved channels.
Configure vulnerability scanners for authenticated scanning using the provided credentials.
Execute authenticated scans against device interfaces.
Review and document scan results, noting additional findings compared to unauthenticated scans.

test_cases.title: Vulnerability Validation
methodology: Review vulnerability scan results from both authenticated and unauthenticated scans.
Confirm true positive findings through manual validation and evidence collection.
Perform targeted manual testing for indeterminate or ambiguous scanner findings.
Document validated vulnerabilities with supporting evidence.

test_cases.title: Network Protocol Cryptographic Analysis
methodology: Identify encrypted protocols in use from captured network traffic.
Run sslscan or equivalent tools against all TLS-enabled endpoints on the device.
Filter captured traffic for TLS ClientHello and Certificate messages to supplement active scanning.
Extract SNI, ALPN, supported TLS versions, and offered cipher suites from both active scans and passive captures.
Flag legacy CBC cipher suites, weak TLS versions, expired certificates, and identity leakage.
Confirm that strong TLS with AEAD-only cipher suites is enforced.
Evaluate cryptographic implementations against current best practices and standards.
Document the overall cryptographic posture of device network communications.

test_cases.title: Verify Ethernet Security Controls Cannot be Downgraded
methodology: Attempt to bypass or downgrade network security controls through protocol manipulation.
Evaluate whether physical access enables circumvention of network-level protections.
Confirm the presence and effectiveness of compensating controls.
Document any successful downgrade paths or bypass methods.

test_cases.title: Sensitive Data Leaked Over Display
methodology: Connect an external monitor via HDMI, DVI, SDI, or DisplayPort to exposed display outputs.
Observe display output during device boot, normal operation, and shutdown phases.
Identify any sensitive data, diagnostic information, or internal system details visible on the external display.
Document all observed data leakage through the display interface.

test_cases.title: Device Display Disruption via External Input
methodology: Connect a tester-controlled laptop to the device display port.
Configure the laptop to duplicate or extend the display.
Observe the device primary and secondary displays for disruption, artifacts, or unexpected behavior.
Document any operational impact from external display input.

test_cases.title: CEC Protocol Detection
methodology: Connect a USB-CEC adapter with appropriate cables to the device HDMI interface.
Scan for CEC-enabled devices on the HDMI bus.
Determine whether the device responds to CEC commands or exposes CEC control surfaces.
Document any CEC-enabled functionality and potential attack vectors.

test_cases.title: Read RFID Tag
methodology: Install RFID interaction tools (Proxmark3, Chameleon, or equivalent).
Perform tag identification using low-frequency and high-frequency searches (lf search, hf search, GETUID).
Attempt to read, extract, and clone tag data from identified RFID tags.
Document tag type, data contents, and security protections observed.

test_cases.title: Snoop RFID Pairing
methodology: Position the RFID sniffing device near the target reader during normal tag interaction.
Perform passive sniffing of RFID communication (iso14443a_sniff, iso14443b_sniff, or equivalent).
Analyze captured data for credentials, authentication keys, and replay opportunities.
Document the security of the RFID pairing and authentication process.

test_cases.title: CAN Bus Traffic Capture
methodology: Add a CAN USB adapter to the bus via a passive splitter or unused connector.
Use an oscilloscope to determine the CAN bus bitrate if unknown.
Configure the CAN adapter with the determined baud rate.
Capture CAN traffic during device initialization, idle, and normal operation.
Try different baud rates if no valid traffic is observed.
Document all captured CAN frames and message identifiers.

test_cases.title: CAN Bus Traffic Replay / Injection / Fuzzing
methodology: Connect a CAN adapter at the determined baud rate.
Send well-known CAN messages, previously captured frames, or fuzzed data onto the bus.
Observe device behavior for faults, disruptions, state changes, or safety-relevant responses.
Document any anomalous device behavior resulting from injected traffic.

test_cases.title: Zigbee Packet Sniffing and Interception
methodology: Install Zigbee sniffing software on the tester workstation.
Connect a compatible Zigbee sniffer dongle (CatSniffer, SONOFF, CC2531, or equivalent).
Intercept Zigbee traffic on identified channels.
Determine the encryption status of captured Zigbee communications.
Document observed network topology, device roles, and data exposure.

test_cases.title: Passive Pairing Interception and PIN Recovery
methodology: Flash sniffer firmware to a compatible radio dongle.
Follow the target device by BD_ADDR to capture active advertising and connection traffic.
Force a re-pair event to capture the full pairing exchange.
Run crackle or equivalent tools to attempt link-key or LTK recovery from the captured exchange.
Assess whether the device uses LE Legacy Pairing or LE Secure Connections.

test_cases.title: LE Secure Connections and Association-Model Verification
methodology: Isolate the SMP pairing exchange from captured BLE traffic.
Inspect the AuthReq field for SC (Secure Connections) and MITM protection flags.
Confirm the presence of ECDH handshake via Public Key and DHKey Check PDUs.
Derive the expected association model from the IO capabilities of both endpoints.
Document the pairing security level and any deviations from expected behavior.

test_cases.title: Persistent Bonding — Reconnection Without Re-Pairing
methodology: Capture the initial pairing and bonding exchange between the device and its companion.
Disconnect without forgetting the bond on either side.
Reconnect and capture the reconnection exchange.
Inspect whether the reconnection performs SMP re-pairing or uses direct link-layer encryption with stored keys.
Document the bonding persistence behavior and key management approach.

test_cases.title: Active Man-in-the-Middle Relay
methodology: Stand up a dual-role BLE relay with a central role paired to the real device and a peripheral role impersonating the device to the companion.
Bridge GATT operations between the companion and the real device through the relay.
Observe whether relayed commands produce physical effects on the target device.
Assess the impact of static passkeys on relay feasibility.
Document any successful interception or manipulation of BLE communications.

test_cases.title: Rogue AP / Evil Twin with Captive Portal
methodology: Bring up an access point broadcasting the target SSID configured as OPEN.
Run a DHCP server to assign addresses to connecting clients.
Periodically deauthenticate clients from the legitimate access point.
Serve a captive portal page and log any submitted credentials.
Document client behavior and credential capture results.

test_cases.title: KARMA / MANA Probe-Response Attack
methodology: Configure a MANA-patched hostapd instance on the tester wireless interface.
Enable probe-response to all client probe requests regardless of ESSID.
Allow association to any probed ESSID.
Log credentials and connection attempts from associating clients.
Document which devices are susceptible to probe-response attacks.

test_cases.title: BSS Transition Management Hijacking (802.11v)
methodology: Identify clients associated with the target access point.
Craft an 802.11v BSS Transition Management Request frame pointing to the attacker BSSID.
Transmit the crafted frame and observe whether the target client roams to the attacker AP.
Document client roaming behavior and susceptibility to transition management attacks.

test_cases.title: Client Probe-Request Harvest
methodology: Perform a passive airodump-ng scan on all channels.
Extract probe-request frames with associated MAC addresses and probed ESSIDs.
Report remembered SSIDs broadcast by the target device.
Note whether the device uses MAC address randomization for probe requests.
Document the privacy implications of observed probe behavior.

test_cases.title: WPA3 SAE Transition-Mode Downgrade
methodology: Configure a rogue access point as WPA2-only broadcasting the target SSID.
Deauthenticate target clients from the legitimate WPA3 access point.
Capture EAPOL handshakes from clients connecting to the WPA2 rogue AP.
Attempt offline passphrase cracking against captured handshakes.
Document whether the device is susceptible to WPA3 transition-mode downgrade.

test_cases.title: Wi-Fi Direct / P2P WPS Scanning
methodology: Run wash or equivalent tools to enumerate WPS-enabled and P2P devices in range.
Identify the target device among discovered WPS/P2P endpoints.
Attempt a reaver PIN attack if WPS is found enabled on the target.
Document WPS configuration status and attack feasibility.

test_cases.title: Active Debug Interface Detection
methodology: Inspect integrated circuits for MCU type and debug interface indicators.
Locate JTAG or debug connector footprints on the circuit board.
Research the expected pinout for the identified MCU.
Use a multimeter to map suspected debug pins to the connector.
Connect a debug probe and scan with OpenOCD for active JTAG TAPs.
Document all detected debug interfaces and access status.

test_cases.title: Firmware Exfiltration via Debug Interface
methodology: Use OpenOCD to display available memory banks and regions.
Attempt read_memory and dump_image operations to extract firmware contents.
Use GDB attached via the debug interface to dump firmware from memory.
Review extracted firmware for sensitive data, credentials, and configuration information.
Document the feasibility and results of firmware extraction.

test_cases.title: SWD Debug Port Probing
methodology: Identify SWD (Serial Wire Debug) footprint or test pads on the circuit board.
Probe suspected pads with a multimeter for the idle SWD clock and data signature.
Connect a debug probe wired for SWD (SWCLK, SWDIO, GND).
Run OpenOCD configured with a Cortex-M target definition.
Attempt to read the DPIDR register to confirm debug port presence.
Determine whether the debug interface is active, disabled, or protected.

test_cases.title: UWB Channel Identification and Traffic Interception
methodology: Connect a UWB sniffer to the tester workstation.
Perform a quick scan to identify the active UWB channel configuration.
Track and collect UWB packets on the identified channel.
Review captured packets for unencrypted data, device identifiers, and ranging information.

test_cases.title: UWB Packet Injection
methodology: Prepare a transmit script with the identified UWB channel parameters.
Transmit extraneous UWB data packets on the active channel.
Monitor the target system for any changes in behavior, state, or reported measurements.
Document the system response to injected packets.

test_cases.title: UWB Replay Attack
methodology: Sniff and select a representative UWB packet from captured traffic.
Configure the replay with matching channel and timing parameters.
Replay the captured packet and monitor for a system response.
Document whether the system accepts replayed packets and any resulting state changes.

test_cases.title: UWB Service Disruption
methodology: Transmit UWB packets at a high rate on the active channel.
Monitor the target system for degradation in performance, accuracy, or availability.
Document any denial-of-service conditions or operational impact.
Assess the system recovery behavior after disruption ceases.

test_cases.title: UWB Practical Distance Reduction Attack
methodology: Configure a UWB injection triggered on the synchronization field of legitimate transmissions.
Run the injection over an extended observation period.
Monitor the target system for changes in reported distance or positioning data.
Document any successful distance-reduction effects and their magnitude.

test_cases.title: Data at Rest Analysis
methodology: Remove or interface with internal storage media (SD card, eMMC, flash chip) following approved disassembly procedures.
Mount the storage on a forensic workstation in read-only mode.
Review the filesystem for sensitive data, credentials, configuration files, and patient information.
Evaluate whether data-at-rest encryption is implemented and its effectiveness.
Document all findings related to stored data security.

test_cases.title: Brute-Force Authentication
methodology: Identify all authentication entry points on the device (login screens, PINs, biometric readers).
Enumerate user accounts through approved discovery methods.
Attempt systematic password and PIN guessing within approved attempt limits.
Document account lockout mechanisms, timing delays, and threshold behavior.
Estimate the practical feasibility of brute-force attacks against observed controls.

test_cases.title: Privilege Escalation / Unauthorized Access
methodology: Log in as an unprivileged or limited-access user with approved credentials.
Attempt to access restricted functions, menus, or data beyond the user role.
Attempt to modify account roles or permissions from the unprivileged context.
Attempt to trick the device into granting elevated access through input manipulation or workflow bypass.
Document any successful privilege escalation paths.

test_cases.title: USB Bus-Power Verification
methodology: Insert a USB power meter into each exposed USB port.
Read and record voltage and current values under load.
Confirm readings are within USB specification (approximately 5V +/-5%).
Note any anomalous power draw or voltage levels.

test_cases.title: USB HID Mouse Acceptance
methodology: Insert a standard USB mouse into each exposed USB port.
Observe the device display for cursor or pointer appearance.
Document which ports accept HID mouse input and any resulting interaction capability.

test_cases.title: USB HID Key-Combination Probe
methodology: Connect a USB keyboard to each exposed USB port.
Attempt standard key combinations: Ctrl+Alt+Del, Ctrl+Alt+F1/F2, Ctrl+Alt+T, Alt+Tab, Super.
Observe for shell access, TTY switching, task manager, terminal launch, or kiosk escape.
Document which key combinations produce a response and the resulting access level.

test_cases.title: Rogue USB Credential/SSH Dump
methodology: Configure an approved HID-attack device with an SSH credential dump payload.
Connect the device to each exposed USB port and observe execution indicators.
Review the device loot directory for captured credentials, SSH keys, or system information.
Document any successful credential extraction.

test_cases.title: Rogue USB Reverse Shell
methodology: Configure an approved HID-attack device with a reverse shell payload.
Set up a listener on the tester workstation at the designated callback address.
Connect the HID-attack device to each exposed USB port and monitor for an inbound connection.
Document any successful reverse shell establishment and the resulting access level.

test_cases.title: Rogue USB Network Device
methodology: Connect an approved HID-attack device configured as a network interface or a USB-to-Ethernet adapter.
Check whether the device operating system enumerates the network interface.
Assess whether USB device-class policy enforcement prevents network interface registration.
Document the system response to rogue network device insertion.

test_cases.title: Concurrent / Multiple USB Device Handling
methodology: Connect multiple USB devices simultaneously via hubs to exposed USB ports.
Observe whether the device enforces count or type restrictions on connected devices.
Document device behavior with multiple concurrent USB peripherals.
Note any enumeration limits or device-class filtering.

test_cases.title: External Removable Media Read/Write
methodology: Connect an approved USB storage device to each exposed USB port.
Test read, write, and execute operations on the removable media.
Review group policy or equivalent restrictions on removable media access.
Document which operations are permitted and any enforced restrictions.

test_cases.title: Data Encryption on USB Storage
methodology: Perform the manufacturer-documented data export workflow to USB storage.
Examine the exported data for entropy characteristics indicative of encryption.
Evaluate the encryption implementation, key management, and algorithm selection.
Document whether exported data is encrypted and the strength of the implementation.

test_cases.title: USB-to-Ethernet Adapter Behavior
methodology: Insert a USB-to-Ethernet adapter into each exposed USB port.
Connect the adapter to a tester-controlled bench network.
Observe link negotiation, IP stack behavior, and interface enumeration.
Attempt DHCP and static IP assignment through the adapter.
Document whether the adapter creates a usable network path.

test_cases.title: Verify USB Security Controls Cannot be Downgraded
methodology: Identify and document all USB security controls in place on the device.
Attempt to bypass USB security controls through device class or ID filtering circumvention.
Test whether USB restrictions can be modified, disabled, or subverted through available interfaces.
Document any successful bypass methods and residual risk.

test_cases.title: Default Configuration Testing
methodology: Examine the out-of-box device configuration before any customization.
Confirm that default settings follow secure-by-default principles.
Confirm that no default credentials are present or that defaults have been changed.
Document any insecure default configuration settings.

test_cases.title: Authentication Testing
methodology: Review configured user accounts and authentication mechanisms.
Attempt password guessing with common and default credential lists.
Confirm the presence and effectiveness of account lockout mechanisms.
Determine password complexity requirements and enforcement.
Document authentication weaknesses.

test_cases.title: Session Management Testing
methodology: Determine how the device handles user sessions and session tokens.
Attempt session switching between user contexts.
Attempt to create privileged sessions through manipulation.
Confirm proper logout behavior and session timeout enforcement.
Document session management weaknesses.

test_cases.title: Authorization Testing
methodology: Identify authorization handling mechanisms and role-based access controls.
Attempt unauthorized access to restricted features and data.
Attempt authorization bypass through direct object references or parameter manipulation.
Attempt privilege elevation through available interfaces.
Document authorization weaknesses.

test_cases.title: Business Logic Testing
methodology: Map key device workflows and operational sequences.
Confirm that control requirements are enforced at each workflow step.
Attempt to skip steps, reorder operations, or provide invalid values in workflows.
Document any logic flaws that permit unintended actions.

test_cases.title: Denial of Service Testing
methodology: Identify potential denial-of-service vectors including account lockouts, resource exhaustion, network flooding, application crashes, and data corruption.
Attempt each identified vector within approved test boundaries.
Document device behavior during and after each denial-of-service attempt.
Record recovery time and any manual intervention required.

test_cases.title: Ensure Software is Supported by Vendor
methodology: Review all off-the-shelf software components and their versions.
Confirm that each component is under active vendor support.
Flag any end-of-life or end-of-support components.
Document the support status of all identified software.

test_cases.title: Review Automated OS Patch Management
methodology: Document the device operating system patching process and update mechanisms.
Review currently installed patches and update history.
Confirm that patching procedures are documented in the cybersecurity management plan.
Document any patching gaps or missing updates.

test_cases.title: Review Automated Third-Party Patch Management
methodology: Document the third-party software patching process and update mechanisms.
Review currently installed third-party patches and update history.
Confirm that third-party patching is documented in the cybersecurity management plan.
Document any third-party patching gaps.

test_cases.title: Code Injection / Application Whitelisting Review
methodology: Review application whitelisting configuration (AppLocker, WDAC, or equivalent).
Try running executables from unauthorized directories and locations.
Try adding items to startup or scheduled task locations.
Check for unified write filter or equivalent integrity controls.
Document whitelisting effectiveness and any bypass paths.

test_cases.title: Privilege Escalation
methodology: Attempt to access higher-privilege accounts through available interfaces.
Attempt to access privileged functions from an unprivileged context.
Attempt to modify account roles or permissions.
Check for known operating system privilege escalation vulnerabilities applicable to the installed version.
Document any successful escalation paths.

test_cases.title: Encryption of Data at Rest
methodology: Confirm whether whole-disk encryption is enabled and the algorithm in use.
Confirm that configuration files containing sensitive data are encrypted.
Confirm that stored passwords are hashed using strong algorithms.
Review removable media encryption policies and enforcement.
Document the overall data-at-rest encryption posture.

test_cases.title: Information Disclosure
methodology: Examine the filesystem and databases for development artifacts, debug logs, and temporary files.
Search for exposed cryptographic keys, certificates, and credentials.
Search for patient data, identifiers, or other sensitive information in accessible storage.
Document all instances of information disclosure.

test_cases.title: Operating System Anti-Exploitation Features
methodology: Verify that ASLR is enabled for application processes.
Confirm that Data Execution Prevention (DEP) settings are enforced.
Verify memory integrity and Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity (HVCI) status where applicable.
Document the status of all anti-exploitation features.

test_cases.title: Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Devices
methodology: Test removable media scanning by introducing an EICAR test file on USB storage.
Check for the presence and status of anti-virus or anti-malware software.
Document whether malicious content on removable media is detected and blocked.

test_cases.title: Auto-run Content
methodology: Connect removable storage containing autorun configuration files to exposed USB ports.
Observe whether autorun or autoplay content executes automatically.
Check group policy or equivalent settings for autorun and autoplay configuration.
Document whether autorun is disabled and enforced.

test_cases.title: Code Integrity Controls
methodology: Check Secure Boot status in the BIOS/UEFI configuration.
Check Device Guard or equivalent code integrity settings.
Confirm that a code-signing scheme is implemented and enforced.
Document the overall code integrity posture.

test_cases.title: Host-Based Firewall and Port Filtering
methodology: Run firewall status commands appropriate to the operating system.
Confirm that the host-based firewall is enabled and actively filtering.
Review firewall rules for appropriate restrictiveness.
Document the firewall configuration and any overly permissive rules.

test_cases.title: Hardened OS Configuration Review
methodology: Perform a manual review against applicable CIS benchmarks or STIG checklists.
Confirm that unnecessary services, devices, and accounts are disabled.
Review group policy or equivalent configuration for security hardening.
Optionally run an authenticated configuration scanner for comprehensive coverage.
Document deviations from hardening baselines.

test_cases.title: Verify Application Security Controls Cannot be Downgraded
methodology: Review all application-level security controls in place.
Attempt to subvert, modify, or disable each identified security control.
Look for further attack opportunities exposed by any successful downgrade.
Document any successful control subversion and residual risk.

test_cases.title: DHCP Option Analysis
methodology: Filter captured traffic for DHCP frames (DISCOVER, OFFER, REQUEST, ACK).
Extract DHCP options 12 (Hostname), 55 (Parameter Request List), and 60 (Vendor Class Identifier).
Flag any asset identifiers, hostnames, or vendor strings broadcast on the network wire.
Document information disclosure through DHCP options.

test_cases.title: DNS Behaviour Analysis
methodology: Walk all DNS queries and responses in captured traffic.
Classify DNS resolvers used by the device (local, external, custom).
Enumerate all queried hostnames and domains.
Check for search-suffix anomalies or domain leakage.
Confirm whether DNS traffic uses cleartext or encrypted transport.
Document DNS behavior and any security concerns.

test_cases.title: External-Peer / SNI Map
methodology: Enumerate all external destination IP addresses with associated ports, SNI values, and byte counts.
Annotate each destination with its observed or inferred purpose.
Flag unexpected or undocumented external destinations.
Document the complete external communication map.

test_cases.title: Network Traffic Capture / Man-in-the-Middle
methodology: Set up a man-in-the-middle position using port mirroring, a passive tap, or ARP-based redirection.
Capture traffic during file transfers, management sessions, and data exports.
Analyze captured traffic for encryption status and cleartext content.
Document any unencrypted sensitive communications.

test_cases.title: Packet-Capture Analysis for Sensitive Data
methodology: Generate representative data through the device during active network capture.
Analyze captures with Wireshark, Scapy, tcpdump, or equivalent tools.
Search for cleartext identifiers, credentials, session tokens, and sensitive payloads.
Document all instances of sensitive data in network traffic.

test_cases.title: SSH Service Configuration and Cryptographic Posture
methodology: Run ssh2-enum-algos and ssh-audit against exposed SSH services.
Enumerate supported key exchange, cipher, MAC, and host-key algorithms.
Test for Terrapin vulnerability and strict key exchange support.
Assess rate-limiting and brute-force protections on the SSH service.
Flag weak or deprecated algorithms.
Document the SSH cryptographic posture.

test_cases.title: SFTP Transmission Security
methodology: Capture network traffic during an SFTP file transfer operation.
Confirm that the entire transfer is encrypted end-to-end.
Verify that no plaintext payload is visible in the captured traffic.
Document SFTP transmission security status.

test_cases.title: SMB Transmission Security
methodology: Capture network traffic during SMB file access or share operations.
Confirm that SMB encryption is active for the captured sessions.
Run netexec or equivalent tools for SMB configuration review (signing, dialect, guest access).
Document SMB transmission security status and configuration.

test_cases.title: ARP / Traffic Poisoning and MITM Resilience
methodology: Conduct ARP spoofing and traffic redirection on internal network segments.
Attempt to interpose between the device and its network peers.
Observe for cleartext data capture, credential interception, or traffic injection opportunities.
Document the device resilience to ARP poisoning and MITM attacks.
